questions.question: Why should data literacy be part of AI training before a model is selected?
options: Because model selection is never important
Because teams need to know whether sources are allowed, fresh, representative, and good enough
Because all internal documents are automatically safe
Because evaluation can be skipped when data is available
questions.explanation: AI feasibility depends on source quality, ownership, permissions, and evaluation before model choice becomes meaningful.

questions.question: Which signal is explicitly part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Stale data is one of the readiness signals used by the artifact.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked plan with category, score, priority, controls, and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact is a lightweight triage planner for classroom and project use.

questions.question: Which control belongs to the lesson design?
questions.explanation: A source inventory helps teams make the evidence base explicit.

questions.question: When should a data scenario become a launch-gate discussion?
options: When impact, uncertainty, and data risk signals are high
Only when the UI is finished
Only when the model is open source
questions.explanation: High-risk data conditions require stronger controls before launch.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the reusable worksheet?
options: To make data assumptions visible enough for teams to challenge and improve them
To hide quality gaps from stakeholders
To approve every use case automatically
questions.explanation: The worksheet creates a practical shared artifact for discovery and pilot planning.
